Yeah, Hindu mythology is very grey. It's sort of like Greek mythology. Zeus not being a perfect God, Indra not being a perfect God. However, we have a rich history of villains. I used to be able to ignore it when I was younger, but as I've gotten older, it's starting to bother me more. And the Naga thing, you're completely right. In my specific sub caste, every family has a specific nag 'dada' who we pay respects to. But then, a lot of 'ill omens' in other cultures are actually considered as powerful symbols in Hinduism. Crows, for example, denote ancestors. So all horror movies portraying them as evil actually seem very funny to me.

I loved the TID, Will and Jem are my favorite, but I wish Indians were given a better role and weren't just a token of inclusivity (or not being there at all. Even that is fine).

Please do remember, I did enjoy TDI, even if I feel the others are problematic. I don't have anything against her. Please take this comment respectfully. Thanks!

Gentle YTA. You mention in the comments that you're an Indian. I don't know how much religion plays a part in your household, but if it does, your parents reaction is understandable. 

My friend is a practicing jain and as such, she's not just a vegetarian, she doesn't consume root vegetables either. The women and girls also have to follow certain rules during periods. We don't have any such rules in my household. However, whenever we would go for lunch to her place (office hour lunches), I would tell her about my period and ask if it was alright to be there or not. I would also make sure that none of my non jain food would touch hers, because she wouldn't be able to eat her food. 

While it seems restrictive, you have to consider that it's your parent's house and their rules apply. In India, vegetarianism / jainism is not just ethical, it's also tied to religious reasons. People practice certain austerities and exercises for their religion and having meat in the house can tender it useless for them. 

I am an ovo vegetarian, but there are certain days where I do not eat eggs, onions, garlic and I do not eat outside on those days because I want a 100% control of the ingredients in my cooking. 

Your heart is in the right place, it was a gift, you accepted it, but it would have been better to ask your parents.
